about: How a presenter deck's slide titles are fitted, by the presentation profile's `titles` knob. `free` is the shipped fitting: a title cut at a clause boundary past a character budget, else at a word with an ellipsis. A named style bounds a title in words and characters and never truncates one mid-clause: a title that does not fit is shortened by choosing a shorter clause of the same sentence, or by cutting a trailing phrase that carries no figure, and when nothing fits the slide is titled from its lead fact's template. It also sets typographic rules: characters a title may not carry and what replaces them. `presenter.lint_titles` refuses a title that breaks its style.

free.about: The shipped titles: up to 92 characters, cut at a clause boundary or with an ellipsis.

reader.about: At most twelve words and eighty characters; no dash or ellipsis (a dash between clauses reads as a colon, or as a comma when the title already has one); never truncated.
